| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name IN ("claude.exe","Claude.exe","cursor.exe","Cursor.exe","code.exe","Code.exe","codex.exe","claude-code.exe") OR Processes.process_name IN ("node.exe","npm.cmd","npx.cmd") AND Processes.parent_process_name IN ("claude.exe","Claude.exe","cursor.exe","Cursor.exe","code.exe","Code.exe","codex.exe","claude-code.exe")) AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe","node.exe","npm.cmd","npx.cmd","curl.exe","wget.exe") by _time, Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where match(process, "(?i)(Invoke-Expression|IEX\s*\(|DownloadString|Net\.WebClient|curl\s+[^|]+\|\s*(sh|bash)|wget\s+-O\s*-|node\s+-e|base64\s+-d\s*\|\s*(sh|bash)|bash\s+-c\s+\$\(|powershell\s+-(e|enc|c)\s|advisory-tracker)") | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime) | sort - lastTime
AI coding agent descendant reading developer credentials / env (Agentjacking credential access) AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts the Agentjacking credential_access stage where the hijacked AI agent's child process dumps environment variables and reads developer secret files — the specific data Tenet showed exfiltrated (env vars, git credentials, private repo URLs, AWS/cloud keys, npm _authToken, .env contents). Independent of the exfil IOC so it survives C2 rotation. Rationale: Tenet's writeup explicitly names the exfiltrated data classes — environment variables, Git credentials, private repository URLs, developer identities — which directly map to the file/env paths in this query. By anchoring on AI-coding-agent parents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex) reading these specific resources, the detection survives even if the attacker rotates the advisory-tracker.com IOC. SENTRY_DSN is included because that's the bootstrap secret a typosquat would harvest first. Cross-checked against: • https://tenetsecurity.ai/blog/agentjacking-coding-agents-with-fake-sentry-errors/ • https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/news/agentjacking-attacks-hijack-ai/ • https://github.com/PSPDFKit/sentry-npm-typosquat-2026-06-iocs
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1552.004 T1555 T1083
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer legitimately asking Claude/Cursor to debug a git auth failure (printenv / git config --get)
  • AI agent reading .npmrc _authToken to scope a sanctioned npm install
  • aws-cli / gcloud-cli config inspection invoked at developer request
  • ohmyzsh / shell-init scripts that printenv on session start under an agent terminal
  • CI emulator running inside Cursor terminal that dumps env for build context
Suppression filter
| where not(ProcessCommandLine has_any ("git config --global credential.helper","git config --get user.email","aws configure list","gcloud auth list")) and not(InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "--debug-auth")
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm parent chain (Claude/Cursor/Codex/node → shell → cred read) and verify the command-line wasn't a developer-issued debug step. Pull the Sentry MCP tool-call history for the developer's session and locate the issue body whose 'Resolution' text seeded the command. 2) Contain: rotate every credential whose file or env-var was read — git PAT, AWS/GCP CLI keys, SSH private keys, .env secrets, npm _authToken, the Sentry DSN itself. Force the developer to re-auth into all coding sessions and invalidate the host's OS keyring. 3) Hunt: across the dev fleet, find every AI-agent descendant that read the same credential paths in the last 30 days; correlate against outbound traffic from the same process tree to advisory-tracker.com and to any unfamiliar /api/v1/telemetry endpoint; audit the org's Sentry projects for forged issues containing markdown resolution sections.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("claude.exe","cursor.exe","code.exe","codex.exe","claude-code.exe","node.exe","npm.cmd","npx.cmd")
    or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("claude.exe","cursor.exe","code.exe","codex.exe","claude-code.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any (
    "Get-ChildItem Env:","Get-ChildItem env:","ls env:","printenv","$env:",
    "type .env","cat .env","Get-Content .env",
    ".git-credentials","git config --global credential","git remote -v",
    @".aws\credentials",".aws/credentials",
    @".ssh\id_rsa",".ssh/id_rsa",@".ssh\id_ed25519",".ssh/id_ed25519",
    ".npmrc","_authToken","SENTRY_DSN"
  )
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentProcess = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          GrandparentProcess = InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          ChildProcess = FileName,
          ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("claude.exe","cursor.exe","code.exe","codex.exe","claude-code.exe","node.exe","npm.cmd","npx.cmd")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (
    "Get-ChildItem Env:","Get-ChildItem env:","ls env:","printenv","$env:",
    "type .env","cat .env","Get-Content .env",
    ".git-credentials","git config --global credential","git remote -v",
    @".aws\credentials",".aws/credentials",
    @".ssh\id_rsa",".ssh/id_rsa",@".ssh\id_ed25519",".ssh/id_ed25519",
    ".npmrc","_authToken","SENTRY_DSN"
  )
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0f

author: Clankerusecase

detection:

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`

| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes

          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process

OAuth consent / suspicious app grant Actions on Objectives High

Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication CloudAppEvents

| where Timestamp > ago(7d)

          ActivityObjects, IPAddress, UserAgent

AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName has "Consent to application"
| where Result =~ "success"
| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName),
         AppId   = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].id),
         User    = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, User, AppName, AppId, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Rethinking MDR as Attackers and Defenders Embrace AI

The Hacker News
2026-06-12 9 use cases 6 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

For most of the past decade, managed detection and response was the answer to a real problem. Security teams couldn't staff around the clock, couldn't hire enough analysts, and needed someone else to handle the alert queue. MDR stepped in. It worked well enough. Until now. The threat landscape has changed faster than the MDR model can adapt. Attackers are using AI to move faster, generate more

Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc

            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code.
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement

// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.

| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-35273")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,

DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-35273")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,

| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("f02a924c9ff92a8780ce812511341182c6b509d45bc59f3f7b522e37225d24fc", "d83fdb9e53c5ff03c4cb0451ea1bebd79b53f29eadc1e2fa394c7af13a86ce2f", "c7e9332731b06644fc73e0046a2a89eaa59b09f54250e9bd622467187351711f", "68257a6f9ff196179ec03624e849927f26599eb180a7c82e14ef5bc4e93bc309", "2ab684d93c1553fad87041b4dea97188a97e78589deee2a7bacff905564f3a35") or SHA1 in~ ("f02a924c9ff92a8780ce812511341182c6b509d45bc59f3f7b522e37225d24fc", "d83fdb9e53c5ff03c4cb0451ea1bebd79b53f29eadc1e2fa394c7af13a86ce2f", "c7e9332731b06644fc73e0046a2a89eaa59b09f54250e9bd622467187351711f", "68257a6f9ff196179ec03624e849927f26599eb180a7c82e14ef5bc4e93bc309", "2ab684d93c1553fad87041b4dea97188a97e78589deee2a7bacff905564f3a35") or MD5 in~ ("f02a924c9ff92a8780ce812511341182c6b509d45bc59f3f7b522e37225d24fc", "d83fdb9e53c5ff03c4cb0451ea1bebd79b53f29eadc1e2fa394c7af13a86ce2f", "c7e9332731b06644fc73e0046a2a89eaa59b09f54250e9bd622467187351711f", "68257a6f9ff196179ec03624e849927f26599eb180a7c82e14ef5bc4e93bc309", "2ab684d93c1553fad87041b4dea97188a97e78589deee2a7bacff905564f3a35")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("f02a924c9ff92a8780ce812511341182c6b509d45bc59f3f7b522e37225d24fc", "d83fdb9e53c5ff03c4cb0451ea1bebd79b53f29eadc1e2fa394c7af13a86ce2f", "c7e9332731b06644fc73e0046a2a89eaa59b09f54250e9bd622467187351711f", "68257a6f9ff196179ec03624e849927f26599eb180a7c82e14ef5bc4e93bc309", "2ab684d93c1553fad87041b4dea97188a97e78589deee2a7bacff905564f3a35") or SHA1 in~ ("f02a924c9ff92a8780ce812511341182c6b509d45bc59f3f7b522e37225d24fc", "d83fdb9e53c5ff03c4cb0451ea1bebd79b53f29eadc1e2fa394c7af13a86ce2f", "c7e9332731b06644fc73e0046a2a89eaa59b09f54250e9bd622467187351711f", "68257a6f9ff196179ec03624e849927f26599eb180a7c82e14ef5bc4e93bc309", "2ab684d93c1553fad87041b4dea97188a97e78589deee2a7bacff905564f3a35") or MD5 in~ ("f02a924c9ff92a8780ce812511341182c6b509d45bc59f3f7b522e37225d24fc", "d83fdb9e53c5ff03c4cb0451ea1bebd79b53f29eadc1e2fa394c7af13a86ce2f", "c7e9332731b06644fc73e0046a2a89eaa59b09f54250e9bd622467187351711f", "68257a6f9ff196179ec03624e849927f26599eb180a7c82e14ef5bc4e93bc309", "2ab684d93c1553fad87041b4dea97188a97e78589deee2a7bacff905564f3a35")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["f02a924c9ff92a8780ce812511341182c6b509d45bc59f3f7b522e37225d24fc", "d83fdb9e53c5ff03c4cb0451ea1bebd79b53f29eadc1e2fa394c7af13a86ce2f", "c7e9332731b06644fc73e0046a2a89eaa59b09f54250e9bd622467187351711f", "68257a6f9ff196179ec03624e849927f26599eb180a7c82e14ef5bc4e93bc309", "2ab684d93c1553fad87041b4dea97188a97e78589deee2a7bacff905564f3a35"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] File write of Talos top-prevalent malware hash to disk (drop site)
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Article-specific behavioural hunt — A tale of two eras
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Execution of Talos top-prevalent malware (Coinminer VID001.exe / W32.Injector / Dropper.Miner) by hash · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.

Execution of Talos top-prevalent malware (Coinminer VID001.exe / W32.Injector / Dropper.Miner) by hash AIInstallation High
Hunts process executions whose SHA256/MD5 matches the four hashes Talos published as their top-prevalent malware for the week of 2026-06-11, or whose filename matches the named coinminer sample 'VID001.exe'. High-fidelity because matches are exact on hashes Talos has telemetry-confirmed in the wild. Rationale: Uses the exact SHA256 (9f1f11..., 96fa6a..., a31f22...) and MD5 hashes Talos published for Win.Worm.Coinminer::1201, W32.Injector:Gen.21ie.1201, and Win.Dropper.Miner::95.sbx.tg in this newsletter, plus the named filename VID001.exe and the d4aa3e7010220ad1b458fac17039c274_NN_Exe.exe filename pattern that appears twice in the article (suggesting a dropper batch). No external corroboration needed — these are first-party Talos telemetry hashes.
ATT&CKT1059 T1496 T1055
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • IR / malware-analysis VM where an analyst detonates the sample on purpose
  • Red-team engagement using the published Talos hashes as a known-good test corpus
  • Backup software with embedded copies of quarantined malware (rare)
  • A legitimate vendor binary that happens to be named VID001.exe (extremely unlikely — verify via SHA256)
Suppression filter
and not (DeviceName has_any ("sandbox","malwarelab","detonation","-ir-") and InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("cuckoo.exe","procmon.exe","procmon64.exe","any.run.exe"))
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): pull the full process tree on the affected DeviceId — parent of the matching process, child processes, and any DeviceFileEvents for the same SHA256 in the prior 24h to identify the drop site. Confirm the SHA256 against Talos reputation (https://talosintelligence.com/talos_file_reputation). Step 2 (contain): isolate the device via Defender Live Response / CrowdStrike RTR, quarantine the binary at the FolderPath returned, and reset the user's credentials if the integrity level was Medium+ or the parent chain included a browser/email client. Step 3 (hunt): pivot on SHA256 across the org for the prior 30 days; query DeviceNetworkEvents for the same DeviceId for mining-pool TLDs (xmrpool.eu, supportxmr.com, nanopool.org) and non-standard high ports; check DeviceRegistryEvents for Run-key persistence under the same InitiatingProcessAccountName.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where SHA256 in ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507","96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974","a31f222fc283227f5e7988d1ad9c0aecd66d58bb7b4d8518ae23e110308dbf91")
  or MD5 in~ ("2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f","aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9","7bdbd180c081fa63ca94f9c22c457376","38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98")
  or FileName =~ "VID001.exe"
  or FileName matches regex @"(?i)^[a-f0-9]{32}_\d+_Exe\.exe$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, MD5, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where SHA256 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507","96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974","a31f222fc283227f5e7988d1ad9c0aecd66d58bb7b4d8518ae23e110308dbf91")
  or MD5 in~ ("2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f","aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9","7bdbd180c081fa63ca94f9c22c457376","38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98")
  or TargetProcessName endswith @"\VID001.exe"
  or TargetProcessName matches regex @"(?i)\\[a-f0-9]{32}_\d+_Exe\.exe$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, SHA256, MD5
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Talos Top-Prevalent Malware Hash Match (Coinminer / Injector / Dropper.Miner)
id: 8c2f4e1a-7b3d-4f5e-9c1a-2d8b6e5f7a91
status: experimental
description: Detects process creation whose hash or filename matches the Talos top-prevalent malware list for week of 2026-06-11.
references:
  - https://blog.talosintelligence.com/a-tale-of-two-eras/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/19
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1059
  - attack.impact
  - attack.t1496
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_hash_sha256:
    Hashes|contains:
      - '9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507'
      - '96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974'
      - 'a31f222fc283227f5e7988d1ad9c0aecd66d58bb7b4d8518ae23e110308dbf91'
  selection_hash_md5:
    Hashes|contains:
      - '2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f'
      - 'aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9'
      - '7bdbd180c081fa63ca94f9c22c457376'
      - '38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98'
  selection_name:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\VID001.exe'
  condition: 1 of selection_*
falsepositives:
  - Internal IR sandboxing of the sample within an analyst VM
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 (@Hashes:(*9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507* OR *96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974* OR *a31f222fc283227f5e7988d1ad9c0aecd66d58bb7b4d8518ae23e110308dbf91* OR *2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f* OR *aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9* OR *7bdbd180c081fa63ca94f9c22c457376*) OR @Image:(*\VID001.exe OR *\vid001.exe OR *\VID001.EXE))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| (SHA256HashData=/^(9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507|96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974|a31f222fc283227f5e7988d1ad9c0aecd66d58bb7b4d8518ae23e110308dbf91)$/i OR MD5HashData=/^(2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f|aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9|7bdbd180c081fa63ca94f9c22c457376|38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98)$/i OR ImageFileName=/\\VID001\.exe$/i OR ImageFileName=/\\[a-f0-9]{32}_\d+_Exe\.exe$/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, SHA256HashData, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_hash in ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507","96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974","a31f222fc283227f5e7988d1ad9c0aecd66d58bb7b4d8518ae23e110308dbf91","9896a6fcb9bb5ac1ec5297b4a65be3f647589adf7c37b45","2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f","aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9","7bdbd180c081fa63ca94f9c22c457376","38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98") OR Processes.process_name="VID001.exe") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.process_hash Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_hash in ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507","96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974","a31f222fc283227f5e7988d1ad9c0aecd66d58bb7b4d8518ae23e110308dbf91","9896a6fcb9bb5ac1ec5297b4a65be3f647589adf7c37b45","2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f","aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9","7bdbd180c081fa63ca94f9c22c457376","38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98") OR Processes.process_name="VID001.exe") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.process_hash Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
File write of Talos top-prevalent malware hash to disk (drop site) AIDelivery Medium
Hunts the file-system drop of the same Talos prevalent-malware hashes regardless of subsequent execution — catches the staging step before the binary runs (or when it's blocked). The d4aa3e7010220ad1b458fac17039c274_<N>_Exe.exe filename pattern (appearing on two of the three samples) is a strong staging-loader hallmark and warrants its own pivot on the file-event surface, separate from the process-execution UC. Rationale: Pivots on the file-system surface rather than process execution — catches the drop before execution (or when AV blocks the run). Filename pattern d4aa3e7010220ad1b458fac17039c274_<N>_Exe.exe is article-specific: it appears twice in the list (the W32.Injector and Win.Dropper.Miner samples share the same 32-char dropper batch prefix), which is a textbook staging-loader naming artefact and a stronger signal than any single hash.
ATT&CKT1105 T1036.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Defender / CrowdStrike quarantining the sample writes the file to its quarantine vault — InitiatingProcessFileName will be MsMpEng.exe / CSFalconService.exe
  • Analyst saves the IOC sample from Talos's portal to a local malware-research share
  • Backup software re-hydrating a previously quarantined file during restore testing
  • FileOriginUrl pointing to talosintelligence.com indicates a researcher download, not a real infection
Suppression filter
and not InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("MsMpEng.exe","MpDefenderCoreService.exe","CSFalconService.exe","CSFalconContainer.exe","SenseIR.exe","MsSense.exe") and not FolderPath has_any (@"\Quarantine\", @"\Defender\Quarantine\", @"\CrowdStrike\Quarantine\")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): inspect FileOriginUrl and FileOriginIP — if it points to talosintelligence.com or virustotal.com the writer is almost certainly a researcher; otherwise treat as a live infection and pivot to the URL/IP for delivery-channel investigation. Step 2 (contain): isolate the host, quarantine the file at FolderPath, and capture the InitiatingProcessCommandLine of the writing process — that names the delivery vector (browser, mail client, archive utility, LOLBin). Step 3 (hunt): query for the same SHA256 across DeviceFileEvents org-wide for the prior 30d, then query DeviceNetworkEvents on the same DeviceId for connections in the ±15 min window around the file write to identify the download source.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where SHA256 in ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507","96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974","a31f222fc283227f5e7988d1ad9c0aecd66d58bb7b4d8518ae23e110308dbf91")
  or MD5 in~ ("2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f","aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9","7bdbd180c081fa63ca94f9c22c457376")
  or FileName =~ "VID001.exe"
  or FileName startswith "d4aa3e7010220ad1b458fac17039c274_"
  or FileName matches regex @"(?i)^[a-f0-9]{32}_\d+_Exe\.exe$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, MD5, FileOriginUrl, FileOriginReferrerUrl, FileOriginIP, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where TargetFileSHA256 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507","96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974","a31f222fc283227f5e7988d1ad9c0aecd66d58bb7b4d8518ae23e110308dbf91")
  or TargetFileMD5 in~ ("2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f","aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9","7bdbd180c081fa63ca94f9c22c457376")
  or TargetFileName =~ "VID001.exe"
  or TargetFileName startswith "d4aa3e7010220ad1b458fac17039c274_"
  or TargetFileName matches regex @"(?i)^[a-f0-9]{32}_\d+_Exe\.exe$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, EventType, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256, TargetFileMD5, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Talos Top-Prevalent Malware Hash Written to Disk
id: f1a3b8d2-5e9c-4a7b-b2e8-1c4d7f6a3e90
status: experimental
description: Detects file-system write of any of the SHA256/MD5 hashes or filename patterns from Talos's prevalent-malware list for week of 2026-06-11.
references:
  - https://blog.talosintelligence.com/a-tale-of-two-eras/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/19
tags:
  - attack.command_and_control
  - attack.t1105
  - attack.defense_evasion
  - attack.t1036.005
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_hash:
    Hashes|contains:
      - '9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507'
      - '96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974'
      - 'a31f222fc283227f5e7988d1ad9c0aecd66d58bb7b4d8518ae23e110308dbf91'
      - '2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f'
      - 'aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9'
      - '7bdbd180c081fa63ca94f9c22c457376'
  selection_name:
    TargetFilename|endswith:
      - '\VID001.exe'
  selection_dropper_pattern:
    TargetFilename|contains: 'd4aa3e7010220ad1b458fac17039c274_'
  condition: 1 of selection_*
falsepositives:
  - Defender / EDR quarantine staging directory
  - Analyst-driven sample handling on a sandbox host
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 (@Hashes:(*9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507* OR *96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974* OR *a31f222fc283227f5e7988d1ad9c0aecd66d58bb7b4d8518ae23e110308dbf91*) OR @TargetFilename:(*\VID001.exe OR *\vid001.exe OR *\d4aa3e7010220ad1b458fac17039c274_* OR *\D4AA3E7010220AD1B458FAC17039C274_*))
#event_simpleName=FileWritten
| (TargetFileName=/\\VID001\.exe$/i OR TargetFileName=/\\[a-f0-9]{32}_\d+_Exe\.exe$/i OR TargetFileName=/\\d4aa3e7010220ad1b458fac17039c274_/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, TargetFileName, ContextImageFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_hash in ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507","96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974","a31f222fc283227f5e7988d1ad9c0aecd66d58bb7b4d8518ae23e110308dbf91","2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f","aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9","7bdbd180c081fa63ca94f9c22c457376") OR Filesystem.file_name="VID001.exe" OR Filesystem.file_name="d4aa3e7010220ad1b458fac17039c274_*_Exe.exe") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_hash Filesystem.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_hash in ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507","96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974","a31f222fc283227f5e7988d1ad9c0aecd66d58bb7b4d8518ae23e110308dbf91","2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f","aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9","7bdbd180c081fa63ca94f9c22c457376") OR Filesystem.file_name="VID001.exe" OR Filesystem.file_name="d4aa3e7010220ad1b458fac17039c274_*_Exe.exe") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_hash Filesystem.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: LSASS Process Access Outside Microsoft-Signed Tooling
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d04
status: experimental
description: |
    Anything opening lsass.exe with read-memory access that isn't a
    Microsoft signed component (Defender, csrss, etc.) is suspect.
    Mimikatz / Pypykatz / nanodump signature.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1003/001/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1003.001
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: process_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        TargetImage|endswith: '\lsass.exe'
    filter_known_good:
        SourceImage|endswith:
            - '\MsSense.exe'
            - '\MsMpEng.exe'
            - '\csrss.exe'
            - '\svchost.exe'
            - '\wininit.exe'
            - '\services.exe'
            - '\lsm.exe'
            - '\SearchProtocolHost.exe'
    condition: selection and not filter_known_good
falsepositives:
    - Third-party EDR / forensic tools — extend the filter list
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"
        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")
       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"
        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")
       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement Actions on Objectives High
psexec / paexec / smbexec / wmic /node — service install over SMB from remote host.
ATT&CKT1021.002 T1569.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
   or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/node:")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688            // process-create (audit-policy required)
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\psexec.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\psexesvc.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\paexec.exe"
   or (NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe" and CommandLine has "/node:")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: PsExec / SMB Lateral Movement Tooling Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d03
status: experimental
description: |
    PsExec, paexec, smbexec, csexec, remcom — admin-grade tooling that
    pivots over SMB. Pair with `wmic /node:` for the full cluster.
references:

        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,

        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)

let BadHashes = dynamic(["9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974", "a31f222fc283227f5e7988d1ad9c0aecd66d58bb7b4d8518ae23e110308dbf91", "9896a6fcb9bb5ac1ec5297b4a65be3f647589adf7c37b45f3f7466decd6a4a7f", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9", "7bdbd180c081fa63ca94f9c22c457376", "38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent

        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)

        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)

                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )

CodeIgniter4 application fingerprinting via /index.php route patterns AIReconnaissance Medium
Recon hunt for CodeIgniter4 instances exposed to the internet. Identifies CI4's default routing (/index.php/controller/method) and CodeIgniter-marker user agents/headers that precede CVE-2026-48062 exploitation attempts. Rationale: Article identifies CodeIgniter4 (composer:codeigniter4/framework < 4.7.2) as the vulnerable framework. CI4's default routing exposes /index.php/controller/method paths and the framework occasionally emits CodeIgniter-marker headers. The CodeIgniter docs linked in the article describe this routing structure. Cross-checked against: • https://codeigniter.com/user_guide/libraries/uploaded_files.html • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2gr4-ppc7-7mhx
ATT&CKT1592.002 T1595.002
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate CodeIgniter4 application use by employees
  • Internal automated monitoring/uptime checks hitting /index.php health endpoints
  • Search engine crawlers (Googlebot, Bingbot) indexing the application
  • Penetration testing tools (Nuclei, Nikto) authorized by the security team
  • Developer testing during application QA cycles
Suppression filter
| where cIP !in ("<internal_monitor_ip>", "<approved_scanner_ip>") and csUserAgent !has_any ("Googlebot", "bingbot", "UptimeRobot")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Determine whether the targeted hostname maps to a known CodeIgniter4 application in CMDB. Pivot on cIP/RemoteIP — is the source internal, a known scanner, or external? Pull CMDB vulnerability data for that host: is the framework version < 4.7.2? Step 2 (contain): If the source IP is unknown-external AND the destination is an unpatched CI4 instance, block the source IP at the perimeter and add the destination host to a watchlist. Notify the application owner. Step 3 (hunt): Pivot from the source IP to all DeviceNetworkEvents/W3CIISLog records for 14 days. Look for subsequent POST requests to upload endpoints (next UC) and any GET requests to .php files in writable/uploads/ paths.

| where DistinctUris > 3
| order by Hits desc

HTTP POST upload with image MIME-type header but script-extension filename (ext_in bypass) AIExploitation High
Detects the exact CVE-2026-48062 exploit shape: multipart POST upload where the declared Content-Type is image/* but the uploaded filename ends in .php/.phtml/.phar. The ext_in rule trusts the MIME-derived extension, allowing a polyglot shell.php to bypass validation. Rationale: Article quote: 'an uploaded file named shell.php containing GIF-like content could pass validation such as: uploaded[avatar]|is_image[avatar]|mime_in[avatar,image/gif]|ext_in[avatar,gif] because the detected MIME type maps to gif, even though the uploaded filename extension is php.' This UC hunts that exact shape — multipart POST + image MIME header + .php filename — which is highly anomalous outside an attack. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2gr4-ppc7-7mhx • https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/434.html • https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/File_Upload_Cheat_Sheet.html
ATT&CKT1190 T1036.008 T1505.003
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate file-renaming utilities that mislabel content types
  • Browser extensions that mangle Content-Type during upload (rare)
  • Pen testers running an authorized assessment against the CI4 app
  • Misconfigured mobile client SDKs uploading thumbnails with wrong extension
  • Developer testing CVE-2026-48062 patch validation in non-prod
Suppression filter
| where SourceIP !in ("<approved_scanner_ip>", "<dev_test_ip>") and DeviceVendor in ("Imperva", "F5", "Cloudflare", "Akamai", "AWS", "Fortinet", "Microsoft")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Pull the full multipart body from the WAF log (FileName, FileType, Message). Confirm the filename extension is genuinely .php/.phtml/.phar and the declared MIME is image/*. Identify the target host — is the CodeIgniter4 framework version < 4.7.2? Step 2 (contain): Block the source IP at the WAF; quarantine the destination web host; preserve the request body and any file written to disk for forensics. If CI4 < 4.7.2 confirmed, take the upload endpoint offline pending patch. Step 3 (hunt): Search DeviceFileEvents/ImFileEvent on the destination for any .php file created in writable/uploads/ or public/uploads/ within +/-10 min of the POST. Pivot on file hash to find every other host that received the same payload. Search subsequent GET requests to that .php filename — those are web-shell invocations.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| where RemoteUrl matches regex @"(?i)\.(php|phtml|phar|php5|php7)([\?]|$)"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("curl.exe", "wget.exe", "powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "python.exe", "python3.exe", "java.exe", "node.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("multipart/form-data", "Content-Type: image/", "@filename=")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where RequestMethod == "POST"
| where isnotempty(FileName)
| where FileName matches regex @"(?i)\.(php|phtml|phar|php5|php7)$"
| where Message has_any ("image/gif", "image/jpeg", "image/png", "Content-Type: image") or RequestContext has_any ("image/gif", "image/jpeg", "image/png") or FileType has_any ("image/gif", "image/jpeg", "image/png")
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, SourceIP, SourceUserName, DestinationHostName, RequestURL, RequestMethod, FileName, FileType, Message, RequestContext
| order by TimeGenerated desc

PHP polyglot file written to web-accessible CodeIgniter4 uploads directory AIInstallation High
Detects creation of .php/.phtml/.phar files inside CodeIgniter4's writable/uploads, public/uploads, or wwwroot/uploads directories. Under CVE-2026-48062, ext_in validation bypass allows a shell.php disguised as a GIF to land in these dirs unaltered when $file->move($path) preserves the client filename. Rationale: Article quote: 'save uploaded files using the original client filename: $file->move($path), store uploads in a web-accessible directory, and allow PHP or other executable files to run from that directory.' This UC catches step 2-3 of that chain. The CI4 docs link in the article confirms writable/uploads is the canonical upload location. Cross-checked against: • https://codeigniter.com/user_guide/libraries/uploaded_files.html#moving-files • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2gr4-ppc7-7mhx • https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/434.html
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1036.008 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • CI4 framework updates dropping legitimate PHP files via Composer
  • Developer/sysadmin restoring web shells from backup for forensic analysis
  • WordPress/Joomla migration utilities copying PHP files into the same shared volume
  • CI/CD deployment writing legitimate application PHP files into the upload mount
  • Penetration testing engagement
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("composer.phar", "composer.exe", "git.exe", "msiexec.exe") and InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Pull file SHA256 and pivot to VirusTotal/sandbox for verdict. Read the first 64 bytes — does the file start with GIF87a/GIF89a/FFD8FF/89504E47 (image magic bytes) followed by `<?php` later in the body? That's the polyglot. Identify the InitiatingProcessFileName — was the write by php-fpm/httpd/w3wp (suspicious) or a developer tool? Step 2 (contain): Quarantine the file (delete or chmod 000), block the source IP that triggered the upload, and disable execution in the uploads directory via .htaccess/web.config/nginx location block. Step 3 (hunt): Search DeviceProcessEvents for any process spawned by php-fpm/httpd/w3wp/nginx in the next 24h whose ProcessCommandLine or parent path includes the dropped filename. Pivot on the file hash to find every other host hit. Audit CodeIgniter4 version across the fleet; force-upgrade < 4.7.3.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType == "FileCreated"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\writable\uploads\", "/writable/uploads/", @"\public\uploads\", "/public/uploads/", @"\inetpub\wwwroot\uploads\", "/htdocs/uploads/", "/var/www/html/uploads/")
| where FileName matches regex @"(?i)\.(php|phtml|phar|php5|php7|inc|pht)$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, FileSize, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType == "FileCreated"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\writable\uploads\", "/writable/uploads/", @"\public\uploads\", "/public/uploads/", @"\inetpub\wwwroot\uploads\", "/htdocs/uploads/", "/var/www/html/uploads/")
| where TargetFileName matches regex @"(?i)\.(php|phtml|phar|php5|php7|inc|pht)$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256, TargetFileSize, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername
| order by TimeGenerated desc

PHP file dropped in CI4 uploads directory then immediately executed by web server AIActions on Objectives High
Correlation detection: a .php file is written into a CodeIgniter4 upload directory, and within 30s the web server (php-fpm/httpd/w3wp/nginx) spawns a shell or recon binary as a child. Matches CVE-2026-48062 post-exploit: shell.php uploaded, then HTTP GET triggers PHP to fork cmd/sh/whoami. Rationale: Article quote: 'In those conditions, this may lead to arbitrary code execution.' That ACE happens when the uploaded shell.php is invoked over HTTP — php-fpm/httpd executes the polyglot, which forks a shell for recon. The 30s window tightly couples upload to first execution, which is the strongest signal that the upload was malicious rather than benign content. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2gr4-ppc7-7mhx • https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/434.html
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1059 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate PHP application that intentionally exec's shell (image conversion via ImageMagick, ffmpeg wrapper)
  • Pen-test of the just-deployed CI4 patch validation
  • Developer running diagnostic PHP scripts in dev/staging that exec whoami
  • WordPress/CMS plugins that shell out to system binaries (ClamAV scan, gif optimization)
  • Backup utilities running PHP-driven file sweeps
Suppression filter
| where ChildProcess !in~ ("convert.exe", "ffmpeg.exe", "clamscan.exe") and AccountName !endswith "$"
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Read the DroppedFile contents — confirm polyglot (image magic + `<?php`). Pull the DelaySec — sub-5s strongly suggests the attacker triggered it; 20-30s suggests scanner or automated PoC. Pivot on WebServer's SourceIP from web logs for the corresponding GET. Step 2 (contain): Kill the ChildProcess (DeviceProcessEvents has ProcessId), quarantine DroppedFile, isolate the host from network if shell egress observed. Block source IP at perimeter. If CI4 < 4.7.3, take the upload endpoint offline. Step 3 (hunt): Pull all DeviceNetworkEvents for the ChildProcess for 7 days — outbound C2? Pull all DeviceFileEvents in the upload dir for 30d to find every other dropped polyglot. Audit the database (mysqld/mariadb) for new admin accounts created by the web shell.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let WindowSeconds = 30;
let UploadDirs = dynamic([@"\writable\uploads\", "/writable/uploads/", @"\public\uploads\", "/public/uploads/", @"\inetpub\wwwroot\uploads\", "/var/www/html/uploads/"]);
let WebServers = dynamic(["php-fpm.exe", "php-cgi.exe", "httpd.exe", "w3wp.exe", "nginx.exe", "apache2", "httpd", "php-fpm", "nginx"]);
let ShellChildren = dynamic(["cmd.exe", "powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "wscript.exe", "cscript.exe", "sh", "bash", "dash", "nc.exe", "ncat.exe", "whoami.exe", "net.exe", "systeminfo.exe", "curl.exe", "wget.exe", "whoami", "id", "uname"]);
let FileWrites = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where ActionType == "FileCreated"
    | where FolderPath has_any (UploadDirs)
    | where FileName matches regex @"(?i)\.(php|phtml|phar|php5|php7)$"
    | project FileWriteTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, DroppedFile = strcat(FolderPath, FileName), DropperProc = InitiatingProcessFileName;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any (WebServers)
| where FileName has_any (ShellChildren) or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("whoami", "uname -a", "id;", "cat /etc/passwd", "net user", "hostname")
| join kind=inner FileWrites on DeviceId
| where Timestamp between (FileWriteTime .. FileWriteTime + WindowSeconds * 1s)
| project FileWriteTime, ExecTime = Timestamp, DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, FileWriteTime), DeviceName, DroppedFile, DropperProc, WebServer = InitiatingProcessFileName, ChildProcess = FileName, ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine, AccountName
| order by ExecTime desc
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let WindowSeconds = 30;
let UploadDirs = dynamic([@"\writable\uploads\", "/writable/uploads/", @"\public\uploads\", "/public/uploads/", @"\inetpub\wwwroot\uploads\", "/var/www/html/uploads/"]);
let WebServers = dynamic(["php-fpm.exe", "php-cgi.exe", "httpd.exe", "w3wp.exe", "nginx.exe", "apache2", "httpd", "php-fpm", "nginx"]);
let ShellChildren = dynamic(["cmd.exe", "powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "wscript.exe", "cscript.exe", "sh", "bash", "dash", "nc.exe", "whoami.exe", "net.exe"]);
let FileWrites = ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where EventType == "FileCreated"
    | where TargetFilePath has_any (UploadDirs)
    | where TargetFileName matches regex @"(?i)\.(php|phtml|phar|php5|php7)$"
    | project FileWriteTime = TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, DroppedFile = TargetFilePath;
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where ParentProcessName has_any (WebServers)
| where TargetProcessName has_any (ShellChildren) or TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("whoami", "uname -a", "id;", "cat /etc/passwd")
| join kind=inner FileWrites on DvcHostname
| where TimeGenerated between (FileWriteTime .. FileWriteTime + WindowSeconds * 1s)
| project FileWriteTime, ExecTime = TimeGenerated, DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', TimeGenerated, FileWriteTime), DvcHostname, DroppedFile, WebServer = ParentProcessName, ChildProcess = TargetProcessName, ChildCmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername
| order by ExecTime desc
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ParentBaseFileName=/(php-fpm|php-cgi|httpd|w3wp|nginx|apache2)(\.exe)?$/i
| ImageFileName=/(cmd|powershell|pwsh|sh|bash|nc|ncat|whoami|net)\.exe$|\/(sh|bash|dash|nc|whoami|id|uname)$/i
| join({#event_simpleName=FileWritten | regex("(?i)(/writable/uploads/|\\\\writable\\\\uploads\\\\|/public/uploads/|\\\\public\\\\uploads\\\\)", field=TargetFileName) | TargetFileName=/\.(php|phtml|phar)$/i}, field=aid, include=[TargetFileName])
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, TargetFileName], function=count())

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as procTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name="php-fpm.exe" OR Processes.parent_process_name="php-cgi.exe" OR Processes.parent_process_name="httpd.exe" OR Processes.parent_process_name="w3wp.exe" OR Processes.parent_process_name="nginx.exe" OR Processes.parent_process_name="apache2" OR Processes.parent_process_name="httpd" OR Processes.parent_process_name="php-fpm") (Processes.process_name="cmd.exe" OR Processes.process_name="powershell.exe" OR Processes.process_name="pwsh.exe" OR Processes.process_name="sh" OR Processes.process_name="bash" OR Processes.process_name="nc.exe" OR Processes.process_name="whoami.exe" OR Processes.process_name="net.exe" OR Processes.process_name="wscript.exe" OR Processes.process_name="cscript.exe") by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.process_id
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| join type=inner dest [
    | tstats `summariesonly` min(_time) as fileTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.action=created (Filesystem.file_path="*/writable/uploads/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\writable\\uploads\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/public/uploads/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\public\\uploads\\*") by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.file_name

    | where match(file_name, "(?i)\.(php|phtml|phar)$")
  ]
