AWS S3 DeleteBucket targeting a CloudTrail log destination bucket AIActions on Objectives High
Detects deletion of an S3 bucket that is — or recently was — the destination for a CloudTrail trail. The article describes attackers with `s3:DeleteBucket` (plus `s3:DeleteObject` to empty it) destroying the long-term forensic store; after deletion the trail's configuration shows the bucket is gone. Rationale: The article calls out `s3:DeleteBucket` + `s3:DeleteObject` against the trail destination as Technique 2, with explicit screenshot of the trail showing the destination bucket missing. Naming-pattern heuristics for log buckets are the article-specific signal; pair with a known-good list of log buckets in your environment for the highest fidelity.
ATT&CKT1485 T1562.008
Data sourcesChange.All_Changes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Retention migration moving logs to a new bucket then deleting the old one
  • Account decommissioning during an org-wide consolidation
  • Terraform/CDK refactor that recreates the log bucket under a new name
  • FinOps cleanup of stale buckets after a workload sunset
  • Disaster-recovery test bucket cleanup
Suppression filter
| where CallerArn !has_any ("role/AWSControlTowerExecution", "role/OrganizationAccountAccessRole") and UserAgent !has_any ("cloudformation.amazonaws.com", "terraform", "control-tower")
Response runbook
1. Triage: capture BucketName, CallerArn, SourceIpAddress, UserAgent. Check whether the bucket was the active destination for any trail (`aws cloudtrail describe-trails` historical config) and whether a replacement bucket exists. Cross-reference with Config history. 2. Contain: revoke the caller's credentials/session if the action wasn't pre-approved, suspend the bucket-policy modification path, and check S3 versioning/object-lock to determine whether prior log objects can be recovered. 3. Hunt: timeline the window from last successful trail log delivery to bucket deletion; in that gap look at GuardDuty/VPC Flow/Config for IAM key creation, role assumption, exfil to public buckets, and any other Technique 1-5 indicators from the article.
let LogBucketHints = dynamic(["cloudtrail","audit","log-archive","-logs-","securitylogs","loggingbucket"]);
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(24h)
| where Application in ("Amazon Web Services","AWS")
| where ActionType =~ "DeleteBucket"
| extend RawData = parse_json(RawEventData)
| extend BucketName = tolower(tostring(RawData.requestParameters.bucketName)),
         CallerType = tostring(RawData.userIdentity.type),
         CallerArn = tostring(RawData.userIdentity.arn),
         ErrorCode = tostring(RawData.errorCode)
| where isempty(ErrorCode)
| where BucketName has_any (LogBucketHints)
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, CallerType, CallerArn, IPAddress, CountryCode, BucketName, UserAgent
| order by Timestamp desc
let LogBucketHints = dynamic(["cloudtrail","audit","log-archive","-logs-","securitylogs","loggingbucket"]);
AWSCloudTrail
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where EventName == "DeleteBucket"
| where isempty(ErrorCode)
| extend BucketName = tolower(tostring(parse_json(RequestParameters).bucketName))
| where BucketName has_any (LogBucketHints)
| project TimeGenerated, EventName, UserIdentityType, UserIdentityArn, UserIdentityUserName, SourceIpAddress, AwsRegion, BucketName, UserAgent
| order by TimeGenerated desc

AWS CloudTrail DeleteTrail removing the trail configuration AIActions on Objectives High
Detects deletion of an entire CloudTrail trail via the `DeleteTrail` API — a step beyond StopLogging that destroys the trail's configuration including its S3/KMS/CloudWatch wiring. Unlike StopLogging this also removes evidence of how logging was originally configured, making restoration harder. Rationale: Reviewer-flagged: the article focuses on `StopLogging` but `DeleteTrail` is the related higher-impact API that removes the trail config altogether. Detection is a single-eventName match with success filter — extremely low FP; alert-worthy on any IAMUser/AssumedRole caller that isn't in a known IaC allowlist.
ATT&CKT1562.008
Data sourcesChange.All_Changes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • IaC pipeline replacing a trail (DeleteTrail immediately followed by CreateTrail with same name)
  • Control Tower / Landing Zone account adoption renaming trails
  • Migration from individual-account trails to an org-wide trail
  • Retiring duplicate trails after central-trail rollout
  • Test account cleanup during sandbox tear-down
Suppression filter
| where CallerArn !has_any ("role/AWSControlTowerExecution", "role/OrganizationAccountAccessRole", "role/TerraformExecutionRole") and UserAgent !has_any ("cloudformation.amazonaws.com", "terraform", "control-tower")
Response runbook
1. Triage: was a replacement CreateTrail seen within ~5 minutes from the same caller? If yes and from an IaC role, likely benign rotation. If no replacement or a different caller, escalate. Capture CallerArn, SourceIpAddress, UserAgent. 2. Contain: re-create the trail with the prior configuration (pull from Config history if available) and re-enable logging; revoke caller's credentials if unauthorised. 3. Hunt: in the trail-blind window, pivot to alternative telemetry (Config, GuardDuty, VPC Flow, application logs, Defender for Cloud) for IAM persistence, KMS key changes, S3 data movement, federation-IdP creation, and any other Technique 1-5 indicators.
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(24h)
| where Application in ("Amazon Web Services","AWS")
| where ActionType =~ "DeleteTrail"
| extend RawData = parse_json(RawEventData)
| extend TrailName = tostring(RawData.requestParameters.name),
         CallerType = tostring(RawData.userIdentity.type),
         CallerArn = tostring(RawData.userIdentity.arn),
         ErrorCode = tostring(RawData.errorCode)
| where isempty(ErrorCode)
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, CallerType, CallerArn, IPAddress, CountryCode, TrailName, UserAgent
| order by Timestamp desc
AWSCloudTrail
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where EventName == "DeleteTrail"
| where isempty(ErrorCode)
| extend TrailName = tostring(parse_json(RequestParameters).name)
| project TimeGenerated, EventName, UserIdentityType, UserIdentityUserName, UserIdentityArn, SourceIpAddress, AwsRegion, TrailName, UserAgent
| order by TimeGenerated desc

GCP Cloud Logging sink disabled via logging.sinks.update AIActions on Objectives High
Detects an attacker setting a Cloud Logging sink's `disabled` field to true via the `google.logging.v2.ConfigServiceV2.UpdateSink` method — the GCP equivalent of CloudTrail StopLogging called out in the article. Once disabled, the sink stops routing matching log entries to their destination. Rationale: Targets the article's named GCP technique: `logging.sinks.update` permission used to set the sink's `disabled` field to true (Figure 1 in the article confirms the console message). Filter on `disabled:true` keeps this very low FP — most legitimate sink updates change filter expressions or destinations, not the disable flag.
ATT&CKT1562.008
Data sourcesChange.All_Changes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Planned cost-control pause of a high-volume sink
  • Sink destination migration where the old sink is disabled before deletion
  • SRE pausing a sink during BigQuery quota troubleshooting
  • Org Policy enforcement work that temporarily disables non-compliant sinks
  • Disaster recovery testing of sink failover
Suppression filter
| where Principal !has_any ("@cloudbuild", "@compute-system", "-terraform@", "@gcp-sa-") and Principal !endswith ".iam.gserviceaccount.com"
Response runbook
1. Triage: pull Principal, CallerIp, ProjectId, SinkName, SinkDestination. Identify whether the sink routes security-relevant logs (Admin Activity, Data Access, VPC Flow) or low-value app logs. Check change-management for an approved maintenance window. 2. Contain: re-enable the sink (`gcloud logging sinks update <name> --no-disabled`); if the principal is unauthorised revoke its session and audit recently granted IAM bindings for `logging.sinks.update`. 3. Hunt: during the blind window cross-reference VPC Flow, GCP IAM bindings, Cloud KMS key changes, and Workspace audit for IdP/role abuse; review whether other sinks in the project were also disabled or rerouted.
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(24h)
| where Application in ("Google Cloud Platform","Google Cloud")
| where ActionType has "UpdateSink" or ActionType =~ "google.logging.v2.ConfigServiceV2.UpdateSink"
| extend RawData = parse_json(RawEventData)
| extend SinkName = tostring(RawData.protoPayload.request.sink.name),
         SinkDestination = tostring(RawData.protoPayload.request.sink.destination),
         Disabled = tobool(RawData.protoPayload.request.sink.disabled),
         Principal = tostring(RawData.protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail),
         CallerIp = tostring(RawData.protoPayload.requestMetadata.callerIp),
         ProjectId = tostring(RawData.resource.labels.project_id)
| where Disabled == true
| project Timestamp, Principal, CallerIp, ProjectId, SinkName, SinkDestination, AccountDisplayName, IPAddress
| order by Timestamp desc
// Microsoft Sentinel — auto-derived from the Defender XDR hunt.
// Requires the Microsoft 365 Defender data connector (streams the
// advanced-hunting tables into Sentinel; Timestamp → TimeGenerated).
CloudAppEvents
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where Application in ("Google Cloud Platform","Google Cloud")
| where ActionType has "UpdateSink" or ActionType =~ "google.logging.v2.ConfigServiceV2.UpdateSink"
| extend RawData = parse_json(RawEventData)
| extend SinkName = tostring(RawData.protoPayload.request.sink.name),
         SinkDestination = tostring(RawData.protoPayload.request.sink.destination),
         Disabled = tobool(RawData.protoPayload.request.sink.disabled),
         Principal = tostring(RawData.protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail),
         CallerIp = tostring(RawData.protoPayload.requestMetadata.callerIp),
         ProjectId = tostring(RawData.resource.labels.project_id)
| where Disabled == true
| project TimeGenerated, Principal, CallerIp, ProjectId, SinkName, SinkDestination, AccountDisplayName, IPAddress
| order by TimeGenerated desc

GCP log bucket deletion via logging.buckets.delete (DELETE_REQUESTED) AIActions on Objectives High
Detects the `google.logging.v2.ConfigServiceV2.DeleteBucket` call against a Cloud Logging log bucket. As the article notes, the bucket enters a 7-day DELETE_REQUESTED state before destruction, giving defenders a window to restore — but the deletion itself is the high-fidelity defense-evasion signal. Rationale: Article Technique 2 (GCP variant): `logging.buckets.delete` permission used to delete a log bucket; deletion enters DELETE_REQUESTED state for 7 days. The methodName is a fixed string so this is a deterministic single-event alert. Principal filtering catches unauthorised users vs known IaC service accounts.
ATT&CKT1485 T1562.008
Data sourcesChange.All_Changes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Decommissioning a stale log bucket after migration to a central project
  • Terraform destroy of an ephemeral project's logging infrastructure
  • Org-wide log retention rework consolidating buckets
  • Cleanup of test/sandbox project buckets
  • Cost-control deletion of an unused secondary log bucket
Suppression filter
| where Principal !has "-terraform@" and Principal !endswith "@cloudbuild.gserviceaccount.com" and CallerIp !in ("35.235.240.0/20")
Response runbook
1. Triage: capture Principal, CallerIp, ProjectId, BucketResource. Because GCP holds the bucket in DELETE_REQUESTED for 7 days, immediate restoration is possible via `gcloud logging buckets undelete`. Determine whether the deleted bucket held security-relevant logs. 2. Contain: issue the undelete within the 7-day window; revoke the principal's session and audit recently granted `logging.admin` / `logging.bucketsAdmin` bindings. 3. Hunt: pivot to other techniques described in the article — was a sink also disabled (UpdateSink), is a parallel attacker-owned export sink siphoning logs to an external project, has the KMS CMEK for the bucket been rotated or revoked?
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(24h)
| where Application in ("Google Cloud Platform","Google Cloud")
| where ActionType has "DeleteBucket" and ActionType has "logging"
   or ActionType =~ "google.logging.v2.ConfigServiceV2.DeleteBucket"
| extend RawData = parse_json(RawEventData)
| extend BucketResource = tostring(RawData.protoPayload.resourceName),
         Principal = tostring(RawData.protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail),
         CallerIp = tostring(RawData.protoPayload.requestMetadata.callerIp),
         ProjectId = tostring(RawData.resource.labels.project_id),
         ErrorCode = tostring(RawData.protoPayload.status.code)
| where ErrorCode in ("","0")
| project Timestamp, Principal, CallerIp, ProjectId, BucketResource, AccountDisplayName, IPAddress
| order by Timestamp desc
// Microsoft Sentinel — auto-derived from the Defender XDR hunt.
// Requires the Microsoft 365 Defender data connector (streams the
// advanced-hunting tables into Sentinel; Timestamp → TimeGenerated).
CloudAppEvents
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)

description: Detects deletion of a Cloud Logging log bucket — destroys forensic evidence after a 7-day DELETE_REQUESTED period.

author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/18

  - attack.t1485
logsource:
  product: gcp
  service: gcp.audit
detection:

falsepositives:

level: high
source:gcp.audit @protoPayload.methodName:google.logging.v2.ConfigServiceV2.DeleteBucket -@protoPayload.status.code:(1 OR 7 OR 13 OR 16)
CLOUD
`gcp_pubsub` protoPayload.methodName="google.logging.v2.ConfigServiceV2.DeleteBucket"
| rename protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail as principal, protoPayload.requestMetadata.callerIp as src_ip, protoPayload.resourceName as bucket_resource, resource.labels.project_id as project_id
| where NOT match(principal, "(?i)gserviceaccount\.com$") OR match(principal, "(?i)(compute@developer|cloudservices@cloudservices)\.gserviceaccount\.com")=false

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`

    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"

| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process

HEEx attribute-break injection markers in HTTP/WebSocket payload to /storybook routes AIExploitation High
Hunts requests targeting phoenix_storybook playground URLs (/storybook/*, /live/websocket) whose query/body carries the article's HEEx attribute-break syntax — the literal `psb-assign` LiveView event name, URL-encoded `"{` (%22%7B) or `" injected` (%22 injected) sequences that signal an attacker breaking out of an attribute string to inject an Elixir expression for unsandboxed EEx evaluation. Specific to CVE-2026-8467 — the only Phoenix LiveView event that drives `ExtraAssignsHelpers.handle_set_variation_assign/3` is `psb-assign`. Rationale: Pulled the literal LiveView event name `psb-assign` from the PoC step 3 and the breakout pattern `foo" injected={EXPR}` from §Details — URL-encoded `%22` (") + `%7B` ({) is the wire signature of an attacker escaping the HEEx attribute context. Cross-checked patch commit 56ab8464 on github.com/phenixdigital/phoenix_storybook to confirm `psb-assign` is the only event reaching the vulnerable code path. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/phenixdigital/phoenix_storybook/commit/56ab8464d4375fa52db806148a06cce126ad481d • https://github.com/phenixdigital/phoenix_storybook/commit/e35379dfe2ef1a71b141899e36f431017c55265d
ATT&CKT1190 T1059
Data sourcesWeb Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal dev/QA browsing storybook playground with auto-generated attribute payloads containing curly braces
  • Security scanners (Burp, ZAP, Nuclei) probing /storybook with injection wordlists
  • Phoenix LiveView legitimate URL-encoded JSON state containing %7B/%22
  • Storybook component examples whose own attribute values happen to include `{` or `"` characters
  • Load tests replaying recorded sessions that include the psb-assign event
Suppression filter
| where not (cIP startswith "10." or cIP startswith "192.168." or cIP startswith "172.16.")
| where csUserAgent !has "Burp" and csUserAgent !has "Nuclei" and csUserAgent !has "ZAP"
Response runbook
1. TRIAGE: Pull the full request URL and (if available) body for the hit. Decode the percent-encoding and look for the escape pattern `"...{EXPR}..."` where EXPR resembles Elixir (e.g. `System.cmd`, `:os.cmd`, `File.read`, `Code.eval_string`). Confirm the host actually serves phoenix_storybook by checking the response Content-Type or banner. 2. CONTAIN: If exploitation looks real, block the source IP at WAF/edge, then either remove the storybook route from production (preferred) or auth-gate it with the LiveView `on_mount` hook. Pin phoenix_storybook to >=1.1.0 in mix.lock and redeploy. 3. HUNT: Pivot on the source IP across the last 30d for any other /storybook traffic, then on the server pivot to UC4 (beam.smp spawning OS commands) and check process/file/network for the same time window. Review BEAM stdout/syslog for `EEx`, `CompileError`, or `eval_quoted` traces.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteUrl has "/storybook" or RemoteUrl has "/live/websocket"
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("psb-assign", "%7B%22", "%22%7B", "%22%20injected", "%22+injected")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, LocalIP, LocalPort, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where csUriStem startswith "/storybook" or csUriStem contains "/live/websocket"
| where csUriQuery has_any ("psb-assign", "%7B%22", "%22%7B", "%22%20injected", "%22+injected") or (csMethod in ("GET","POST") and csUriStem contains "/storybook/")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, cIP, csMethod, csUriStem, csUriQuery, scStatus, csUserAgent, csBytes
| order by TimeGenerated desc

HTTP 5xx spike + EEx/CompileError on /storybook routes — failed HEEx injection attempts AIExploitation High
Detects bursts of HTTP 500-class responses from /storybook routes correlated with EEx/CompileError patterns in BEAM application logs — the noisy footprint of failed CVE-2026-8467 injection attempts where the attacker's payload is syntactically invalid HEEx and crashes `EEx.compile_string/2` instead of executing cleanly. Rationale: Article §Details step 3 confirms the unsafe path goes through `EEx.compile_string/2` + `Code.eval_quoted_with_env/3` — Elixir's exception names on failure are `EEx.CompileError` / `CompileError`, and §Details notes the injected expression "executes on the server even if it causes a rendering error" so we should still see 5xx noise on probe runs. The file names `attributes_markup` and `PlaygroundPreviewLive` are pulled verbatim from the article. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/phenixdigital/phoenix_storybook/blob/main/lib/phoenix_storybook/live/playground/playground_preview_live.ex
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate storybook component crashes during dev iteration (CompileError raised by a developer's broken Heex template, not an attacker)
  • Storybook page that intentionally renders raising components for testing
  • Upgrades/redeploys causing transient 502/503 on storybook routes
  • Load tests that intentionally submit malformed psb-assign payloads
  • Phoenix LiveView reconnect storms after network flap returning 5xx in bulk
Suppression filter
| where cIP !startswith "10." and cIP !startswith "192.168." and cIP !startswith "172.16."
Response runbook
1. TRIAGE: Inspect the offending source IP's request URLs around the 5xx burst — decode the payloads and check whether the attribute value contains an attribute-string breakout (the `"{...}` pattern). Pull the matching Syslog/Logger lines to confirm `EEx.CompileError` came from `PlaygroundPreviewLive` / `attributes_markup`, not from a developer's own template. 2. CONTAIN: If the source IP is external and the host is production, block at WAF and remove/auth-gate the storybook route. Confirm phoenix_storybook is upgraded to >=1.1.0. 3. HUNT: Within the same source IP / session ID, look for any psb-assign request that did NOT 5xx (UC1) — that's the successful payload — and chase post-exploitation on the server (UC4: beam.smp spawning OS commands).

Internet-facing host exposes /storybook/* routes (phoenix_storybook attack-surface check) AIReconnaissance High
Surfaces production / internet-facing hosts that have vulnerable phoenix_storybook (>=0.5.0,<1.1.0) installed AND are receiving inbound requests to /storybook/* — the prerequisite attack surface for unauthenticated CVE-2026-8467 exploitation. Combines vulnerability inventory with live exposure check. Rationale: Article §Impact: "All versions of phoenix_storybook from 0.5.0 before 1.1.0 are affected" + "any user able to reach the storybook endpoint, including unauthenticated internet users if the storybook is publicly deployed". Pairing the vulnerable-version inventory with IsInternetFacing and a positive 200/101 on /storybook scopes the alert to actually-reachable installs, not every Erlang server in the fleet. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-55hg-8qxv-qj4p • https://hex.pm/packages/phoenix_storybook
ATT&CKT1190 T1592.002
Data sourcesVulnerabilities.Vulnerabilities Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Marketing / docs site intentionally exposing storybook as a public component gallery
  • Staging host mistakenly tagged IsInternetFacing because of perimeter NAT
  • Dev-tooling demo hosts where storybook is acceptable
  • Phoenix application that has /storybook namespace for a different feature (not the phoenix_storybook library)
  • DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities lag — software was upgraded but inventory not refreshed yet
Response runbook
1. TRIAGE: For each device returned, validate phoenix_storybook version by reading mix.lock or `mix deps` on the host. Confirm IsInternetFacing by checking edge ACLs / cloud SG. 2. CONTAIN: Either remove the `live_storybook` mount from the Phoenix router in prod, or wrap it in an auth pipeline (Plug.BasicAuth or your existing on_mount). Pin phoenix_storybook >=1.1.0 in mix.lock and redeploy. 3. HUNT: Pull /storybook access logs for the prior 30d, geo-bucket source IPs, and look for any psb-assign requests with attribute-break markers (UC1). If found, escalate to incident and pivot to UC4 on the host.

BEAM/Erlang VM (beam.smp/erl.exe) spawning OS commands — post-HEEx-injection code execution AIInstallation High
Detects the unmistakable post-exploitation footprint of CVE-2026-8467: the Erlang VM (beam.smp / erl.exe) — which should almost never directly spawn shell or recon binaries — spawning cmd.exe / powershell.exe / sh / bash / curl / wget / net / whoami. Article confirms the injected expression "executes on the server" via `Code.eval_quoted_with_env/3` with full Kernel — the textbook follow-on is `System.cmd/2` or `:os.cmd/1`. Rationale: Article §Details step 3 confirms `Code.eval_quoted_with_env/3` runs with full `Kernel` imports and §PoC step 3 explicitly cites `System.cmd/2` as the example payload — so the BEAM process (beam.smp on Linux, erl.exe / beam.smp.exe on Windows) becoming the parent of a shell binary is the highest-fidelity confirmation that an HEEx-injection foothold turned into OS command execution. BEAM legitimately almost never spawns these directly; releases run as long-lived servers. Cross-checked against: • https://hexdocs.pm/elixir/System.html#cmd/3
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1059.003 T1059.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Phoenix app legitimately shelling out via System.cmd/2 for thumbnail generation, video encoding, git operations, etc.
  • Releases that exec `epmd -daemon` or other Erlang tooling on startup
  • Health-check Erlang scripts running `ifconfig` / `uname` / `whoami` for diagnostics
  • CI/CD scripts on the same host running mix tasks that spawn shell wrappers
  • Phoenix apps using a port driver that wraps a CLI binary (e.g. erlexec, MuonTrap)
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("thumbnail", "ffmpeg", "imagemagick", "git ", "healthcheck") or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("--healthcheck", "--probe"))
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
Response runbook
1. TRIAGE: Inspect ProcessCommandLine of the child — recon (`whoami`, `id`, `uname -a`, `ipconfig /all`), download (`curl http://`, `wget http://`), reverse shell (`bash -i >& /dev/tcp/...`), or write-to-disk indicate exploitation. Pull the BEAM process command line and confirm it's the phoenix_storybook host. Pivot to UC1 on the same host within the prior 5 minutes for the originating WebSocket payload. 2. CONTAIN: Isolate the host in Defender / cloud SG. Capture memory if feasible (BEAM holds the eval'd quoted form). Kill the BEAM PID only after capture. Rotate any secrets readable by the app user (DB creds, API keys, cloud IAM if instance-profile-attached). 3. HUNT: Search FileWritten in the last 24h for new files in `/tmp`, `/var/tmp`, `priv/`, and DNS / NetworkConnectIP4 from the BEAM PID for C2 beacons. Audit assumed-role / cloud API activity from the host's instance identity for lateral movement.

| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","sh","bash","dash","zsh","wget","curl","nc","ncat","whoami.exe","whoami","net.exe","net1.exe","ipconfig.exe","ifconfig","id","uname")

title: BEAM/Erlang VM Spawning OS Commands (Post HEEx Injection — CVE-2026-8467)
id: 7a3c9d12-5e8b-4f2a-bc1d-9e6f0a4b3c77
description: Detects the Erlang BEAM virtual machine (beam.smp / erl.exe) spawning OS command interpreters or recon binaries — the post-exploitation footprint of HEEx template injection RCE (CVE-2026-8467) in phoenix_storybook.
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-55hg-8qxv-qj4p
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/19
tags:
  - attack.t1059
  - attack.t1059.001
  - attack.t1059.003
  - attack.t1059.004
  - cve.2026.8467
logsource:
  category: process_creation
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\beam.smp.exe'
      - '\erl.exe'
      - '\erts.exe'
      - '/beam.smp'
      - '/erl'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\wget.exe'
      - '\curl.exe'
      - '\whoami.exe'
      - '\net.exe'
      - '\ipconfig.exe'
      - '/sh'
      - '/bash'
      - '/dash'
      - '/zsh'
      - '/curl'
      - '/wget'
      - '/whoami'
      - '/id'
      - '/uname'
  condition: selection_parent and selection_child
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\\beam.smp.exe OR *\\erl.exe OR *\\erts.exe OR *\\BEAM.SMP.EXE OR *\\ERL.EXE) @Image:(*\\cmd.exe OR *\\CMD.EXE OR *\\powershell.exe OR *\\PowerShell.exe OR *\\POWERSHELL.EXE OR *\\pwsh.exe OR *\\PWSH.EXE OR *\\wget.exe OR *\\curl.exe OR *\\whoami.exe OR *\\net.exe OR *\\ipconfig.exe)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ParentBaseFileName=/^(beam\.smp|beam\.smp\.exe|erl\.exe|erts\.exe|epmd\.exe)$/i
| ImageFileName=/(cmd|powershell|pwsh|sh|bash|dash|zsh|wget|curl|nc|ncat|whoami|net|net1|ipconfig|ifconfig|id|uname)(\.exe)?$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count(as=spawns))
| sort(field=spawns, order=desc)
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdlines values(Processes.process_name) as child_procs from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name IN ("beam.smp","beam.smp.exe","erl.exe","erts.exe","epmd.exe")) (Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","sh","bash","dash","zsh","wget","curl","nc","ncat","whoami.exe","whoami","net.exe","net1.exe","ipconfig.exe","ifconfig","id","uname")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdlines values(Processes.process_name) as child_procs from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name IN ("beam.smp","beam.smp.exe","erl.exe","erts.exe","epmd.exe")) (Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","sh","bash","dash","zsh","wget","curl","nc","ncat","whoami.exe","whoami","net.exe","net1.exe","ipconfig.exe","ifconfig","id","uname")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-8467")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-8467")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc
APPLICATION

Auto-generated hunt targeting the specific binaries, paths, registry locations and command-line fragments named in this article. Hunting tier — needs analyst review and environment tuning before promotion to alerting.
ATT&CKT1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Registry
// Article-specific bespoke detection — [GHSA / CRITICAL] CVE-2026-8467: PhoenixStorybook: Unauthenticated remote code e
// Hunts the actual binaries / paths / commandline fragments named
// in the article instead of a generic technique-class template.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (FileName in~ ("system.cmd"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName,
          FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc

// File-creation events for the named binaries / paths
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where (FileName in~ ("system.cmd"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath,
          FileName, ActionType, InitiatingProcessFileName,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc

DeviceProcessEvents

// File-creation events for the named binaries / paths
DeviceFileEvents

``` Article-specific bespoke detection — [GHSA / CRITICAL] CVE-2026-8467: PhoenixStorybook: Unauthenticated remote code e ```
| tstats `summariesonly` count earliest(_time) AS firstTime latest(_time) AS lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process_name IN ("system.cmd"))
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name,
       Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_path
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| append [
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("created","modified")
      AND (Filesystem.file_name IN ("system.cmd"))
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, Filesystem.process_name,
       Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.file_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
]
